## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The invite validator still accepts passwords of 8 to 11 characters, so the twelve-character policy this pull request sets out to enforce is not applied everywhere. This should be fixed. The signup and reset changes are correct, and their boundary tests are sound.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/signup.py:1 — correctness — An 8-to-11-character password such as `"x" * 10` is still accepted through the invite flow, because the diff raises `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH` to 12 only in `app/signup.py` and `app/reset.py` and leaves `app/invite.py:1` at `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 8`. The PR body says this change "raises the minimum in the password validators," but `app/invite.py:5` (`return len(password) >= MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH`) still enforces the old value. In addition, `tests/test_invite.py:6-8` still asserts `length >= 8`, so that test currently treats the old minimum as correct. Recommended fix: set `app/invite.py:1` to 12 and update `tests/test_invite.py` to the `[0, 8, 11, 12, 13]` / `length >= 12` boundaries used for signup and reset. — Users who join through an invite can still set passwords shorter than the twelve-character security policy allows, and the test suite would flag a correct fix to that validator as a failure.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- `tests/test_signup.py:6` and `tests/test_reset.py:6` test lengths 11, 12 and 13, so an off-by-one mistake (`>` instead of `>=`, or a minimum of 11 or 13) would make them fail.
- In each changed module the minimum is a single named constant, and `accepts_password` reads it, so the boundary is set in only one place per module.
